On the final night before the attacks, they lodged at a hotel in Herndon, Virginia, close to the airport.<sup>[[9/11 Commission Report/Notes/Part 7#endnote_189|189]]</sup>

Further north, the hijackers targeting United Airlines Flight 93, to depart from Newark, gathered in that city from their base in Florida on September 7.
Just after midnight on September 8-9, Jarrah received a speeding ticket in Maryland as he headed north on I-95. He joined the rest of his team at their hotel.<sup>[[9/11 Commission Report/Notes/Part 7#endnote_190|190]]</sup>

Atta was still busy coordinating the teams. On September 7, he flew from Fort Lauderdale to Baltimore, presumably to meet with the Flight 77 team in Laurel. On September 9, he flew from Baltimore to Boston. By then, Shehhi
had arrived there, and Atta was seen with him at his hotel. The next day, Atta picked up Omari at another hotel, and the two drove to Portland, Maine, for
reasons that remain unknown. In the early morning hours of September 11, they boarded a commuter flight to Boston to connect to American Airlines Flight 11. The two spent their last night pursuing ordinary activities: making ATM withdrawals, eating pizza, and shopping at a convenience store. Their three fellow hijackers for Flight 11 stayed together in a hotel in Newton, Massachusetts, just outside of Boston.<sup>[[9/11 Commission Report/Notes/Part 7#endnote_191|191]]</sup>

Shehhi and his team targeting United Airlines Flight 175 from Logan Airport spent their last hours at two Boston hotels.<sup>[[9/11 Commission Report/Notes/Part 7#endnote_192|192]]</sup> The plan that started with
a proposal by KSM in 1996 had evolved to overcome numerous obstacles.Now 19 men waited in nondescript hotel rooms to board four flights the next morning.<noinclude></noinclude>
